memory_verse.label: Bible Reference
memory_verse.text: "But the Lord hardened Pharaoh's heart and he would not listen to Moses and Aaron, just as the Lord had said to Moses." - Exodus 9:12 (NIV)

devotion.label: Devotion
devotion.text:
Until now, the text has mostly said that Pharaoh hardened his own heart. Here, for the first time in the plague narrative, it says the Lord hardened Pharaoh's heart.

The order matters. Pharaoh hardened himself again and again, and then God confirmed him in the direction he had chosen. This is not God forcing a good man to sin. It is God's judgement on a man who has repeatedly refused the light he was given.

Paul discusses this very passage in Romans 9, and even he acknowledges it raises hard questions — before reminding us that we are in no position to talk back to God (Rom 9:18-21). Sincere believers who love Scripture have long differed on how divine sovereignty and human responsibility fit together, and this devotional will not settle that debate.

What all can affirm is this: God is perfectly just, He is never the author of evil, no one is ever condemned unfairly, and His purposes stand.

The practical response is not speculation but urgency. Do not delay obedience. Do not treat conviction casually. Today, if you hear his voice, do not harden your heart (Heb 3:15).

reflection.label: Reflection
reflection.text:
1. Is there conviction I have been repeatedly setting aside?
2. Can I trust God's justice in matters I cannot fully understand?

prayer.label: Prayer
prayer.text: Lord, I do not understand everything about Your ways, but I trust Your justice. Keep my heart tender toward You. Amen.
